body_markdown:
Following nearly two centuries of local observances, Thanksgiving was[first celebrated as a national holiday](https://www.si.edu/spotlight/thanksgiving/history) in the United States with a 1789 proclamation by George Washington. Since then, the traditional autumn festival has expanded beyond the dinner table, influencing entertainment and the economy. In some places, though, Thanksgiving looms larger in the popular imagination than in others.


SmartAsset analyzed the 50 states to identify America’s Thanksgiving hotspots. Each state was scored on residents’ Google search interest in Thanksgiving, turkey farms per capita and the number of popular films set in the state that feature Thanksgiving celebrations or autumn family gatherings. The results highlight where the holiday has the strongest presence in economy, culture and popular interest.


## Key Findings


- **New York is America’s No. 1 Thanksgiving hotspot.** The Empire State is the setting for 16 popular Thanksgiving films, including “You’ve Got Mail” (1998), “Hannah and Her Sisters” (1986) and “The Wiz” (1978). Relative Google search interest in the holiday is also high among New Yorkers.
- **New Jersey leads in Thanksgiving search interest.** Garden State residents register the highest relative Google search interest in the holiday, earning a score of 100 out of 100.
- **West Virginia has the most turkey farms per capita.** Although the state ranks No. 26 overall, it leads this metric with 24.2 turkey farms per 100,000 residents. Texas has the largest total number, with 2,427 farms.
- **States with deep Thanksgiving histories rank highly.** Massachusetts, site of[the 1621 observance](https://visit.archives.gov/whats-on/explore-exhibits/thanksgiving-historical-perspectives) traditionally recognized as the nation’s first significant Thanksgiving celebration, ranks No. 2. Pennsylvania, where[the nation’s oldest Thanksgiving parade began in 1920](https://www.britannica.com/question/What-is-the-oldest-Thanksgiving-Day-parade-in-the-U-S) , ranks No. 3. Connecticut, whose colonial government[established a day of general thanksgiving in 1639](https://library.law.uconn.edu/2023/11/18/connecticuts-contribution-to-thanksgiving/) , ranks No. 9.

## Questions and Answers


What is the oldest Thanksgiving parade in the United States?


Philadelphia hosts America’s oldest Thanksgiving Day parade, launched in 1920 by Gimbels department store to promote holiday shopping. After Gimbels closed in 1986, WPVI-TV partnered with various corporate sponsors to continue the tradition.


When was the United States’ first nationwide Thanksgiving observance?


Thanksgiving was first celebrated nationally in 1789 following President George Washington’s proclamation. Prior celebrations were largely local observances. President Abraham Lincoln established it as an annual event in 1863. It became a federal holiday in 1941.


Which U.S. state has the most turkey farms?


West Virginia has the most turkey farms per capita, about 24.2 per 100,000 residents. Texas has the largest total number, 2,427.


What are some popular Thanksgiving films?


Popular films featuring Thanksgiving scenes include “The Gold Rush” (1925), “Holiday Inn” (1942), “Hannah and Her Sisters” (1986) and “Planes, Trains and Automobiles” (1987).


## Ten Thanksgiving Milestones


- **1500s:** Authorities in England[increasingly declare special days of thanksgiving](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-british-studies/article/abs/public-worship-and-political-participation-in-elizabethan-england/536E16BA0239BE448588FEC18A6B5EC0) to commemorate significant events, such as the end of the 1563 plague outbreak, marked by a thanksgiving ordered in 1564. Occasional thanksgivings continued for centuries, but a few — notably May 29 (“Oak Apple Day”) — were made fixed annual observances by statute; the May 29 holiday, marking the Restoration, was repealed in 1859.
- **1621:** The[Pilgrims and Wampanoag observe](https://www.loc.gov/classroom-materials/thanksgiving) what is traditionally recognized as America’s first Thanksgiving celebration, though records exist of prior observances.
- **1777:** The[Continental Congress recommends that states](https://history.house.gov/Blog/2026/March/3-20-Fasting-Thanksgiving) observe December 18 of that year as a national day of Thanksgiving to commemorate the United States victory over British, Brunswick and Hesse-Hanau forces at the Battles of Saratoga.
- **1789:** President George Washington[declares Nov. 26, 1789](https://www.loc.gov/item/today-in-history/november-26) a Thanksgiving holiday, marking the United States’ first presidentially proclaimed Thanksgiving observance.
- **1827:** Sarah Josepha Hale publishes the historical fiction novel “Northwood; A Tale of New England,” in which she describes[an elaborate Thanksgiving dinner](https://www.pilgrimhall.org/the-godmother-of-thanksgiving/) rooted in New England culinary traditions. Hale’s depiction helps popularize the modern Thanksgiving menu.
- **1863** : President[Abraham Lincoln proclaims](https://www.nps.gov/liho/learn/historyculture/lincoln-and-thanksgiving.htm) the last Thursday of November a Thanksgiving observance, beginning an uninterrupted tradition of presidential Thanksgiving proclamations.
- **1876:** What is believed to be the[first Thanksgiving Day game](https://njmonthly.com/articles/news/how-new-jersey-kicked-off-thanksgivings-football-tradition/) of intercollegiate football is played, Yale defeating Princeton by a score of 2-0.
- **1920:** Philadelphia begins staging what becomes[the nation’s oldest Thanksgiving Day parade](https://www.britannica.com/question/What-is-the-oldest-Thanksgiving-Day-parade-in-the-U-S) .
- **1941:**[Congress sets the fourth Thursday of November](https://www.archives.gov/legislative/features/thanksgiving) as a federal Thanksgiving holiday.
- **1989:** President George H.W. Bush[“pardons” a turkey](https://www.whitehousehistory.org/questions/which-president-started-the-tradition-of-pardoning-the-thanksgiving-turkey) , beginning what becomes an annual occurrence. Earlier presidents intermittently issued similar pardons.


## Methodology


Each state was evaluated using three metrics: relative Google search interest in Thanksgiving during November 2025, the most recent complete month available; turkey farms per 100,000 residents; and the number of popular Thanksgiving films set in each state. Google Trends scores range from zero to 100 and reflect Thanksgiving searches as a share of all searches within each state. Turkey farm counts came from the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s 2022 Census of Agriculture — the most recent data available, published in February 2024 — and were adjusted using 2022 state population estimates from StatsAmerica. Thanksgiving films were identified using Rotten Tomatoes’ “[70 Best Thanksgiving Movies](https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/guide/best-thanksgiving-movies) ” list, with each film assigned to its principal setting when possible. The list includes films with Thanksgiving scenes and films featuring nonholiday autumn family gatherings. The three metrics were weighted differently and combined into a composite score used to rank the states.
